name: agent-fs-write-operations
body:
Code-writer implementer agents must be able to delete, move, and copy files inside the surface they own, so a plan task with a `deletes` / `renames` / `moves` verb is implementable. (Historic motivation: the generated implementers carried only shallow bash `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` grants and no `mv`/`cp`.)

The capability is delivered by a small suite of filesystem tools — `apg_rm`, `apg_mv`, `apg_cp` — installed by `apg init`, which SELF-ENFORCE their scope: each tool reads the acting agent's own effective `permission.edit` scope — its ALLOW and DENY entries, evaluated in order with the LAST matching entry winning — from the caller's agent permission block (via the opencode plugin context) and refuses any path not granted by them (a path matched by no entry is refused; deny-by-default), with the rule set and the candidate resolved in one consistent frame. This makes the fs scope EQUAL the agent's `edit` scope: the fs tools can never touch a path the agent's `edit` permission denies (reconciled by `requirements.note.fs-scope-deny-mirror`). The tool-level grant (deny-by-default) is only the callability gate; per-path scoping lives inside the tool. For a code-writer the granted globs are WORKTREE-ONLY — `apg/.worktrees/*/<glob>`, never the repo-root path (amended by `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`): opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the worktree form is what reaches the worktree, and a root grant would make main writable. This is a scoped capability, never a blanket grant: a path outside the agent's granted globs (or revoked by a later deny entry) is refused, a path resolving into the main checkout is refused, and an operation may not cross the project/worktree boundary. The suite tools replace the shallow bash `rm <dir>/*.<ext>` grants.

Scope: rm + mv + cp only. Product source (`opencode-suite/**` tool files, `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts`, `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`) plus the binary's install registry (`rust.apg.install`'s `SUITE_TOOLS`). NOT the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**`. Plain filesystem operations only — no `git rm`/`git mv` — and no change to the binary's node/edge mutation surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- `apg init` installs the three tools into `~/.opencode/tools/`: `rust.apg.install`'s `SUITE_TOOLS` carries one entry per new tool.
- A generated implementer agent is granted `apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp` scoped to exactly its owned path globs under `apg/.worktrees/*/` (worktree-only; no repo-root variant), replacing the shallow bash `rm` grants; the tool self-enforces that scope per path.
- An fs-op whose source path (and, for mv/cp, destination path) is matched by an allow entry with no later deny override succeeds; a path outside the granted entries, or revoked by a later deny entry, is refused.
- The fs tools honour `deny` entries: a DENY entry that is the LAST matching entry refuses the operation, exactly mirroring opencode's `edit` permission (last match wins). A pure unit test over `fsScopeDecision` pins the deny/order semantics; the opt-in boundary e2e pins the frontmatter parse (allow AND deny read as ordered rules).
- An fs-op whose path escapes the project/worktree boundary, or resolves into the main checkout, is refused.
- The install-assertion e2e (`rust.main_e2e.e2e.suite_installs_node_edge_project_tools_and_retires_spec_invariant`) asserts the three tools are embedded and installed, and stays green.
